first_impression: Looks surprisingly authentic to real sheepdog handling rather than just another generic cozy game, backed by lovely typography. The low-poly sheep look a bit stiff like crushed geometric paper, but the sheer variety of herding verbs - creeping, flanking, staring down rams - suggests real mechanical depth.
best_things: Authentic sheepdog trial verbs like creep, lie down, flank, and stare-down that give herding tactical finesse rather than sloppy physics bumping.
The UI and typography are exceptionally clean, stylish, and informative without cluttering the screen.
Every evening introduces a distinct, logical mechanical twist - from stubborn rams and vulnerable lambs to misty navigation and formal show trials.

worst_problems.problem: Keyboard controls look horribly cramped and overmapped (WASD + Shift + C + Q + Z + X + F + Space), demanding awkward finger gymnastics.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add full gamepad support with intuitive twin-stick steering, trigger sprint, and face-button whistles.

worst_problems.problem: The low-poly environment and faceted origami-style sheep models look stiff and asset-pack generic compared to the premium UI and cozy Scottish aesthetic.
worst_problems.suggestion: Soften the polygon edges, add bouncy sheep locomotion animations, and give the terrain more naturalistic foliage shading.

worst_problems.problem: Aggressive wolf pressure and tight countdown timers risk ruining the calm, methodical rhythm of sheep handling with frustrating twitch-reflex panic.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make wolf appearances feel like tactical positioning puzzles rather than frantic countdown scrambles, or expand the 'Gentle' mode leeway.

worst_problems.problem: Fixed high isometric perspective makes navigating narrow bottlenecks like stone wall gates and footbridges awkward to align.
worst_problems.suggestion: Allow camera rotation or subtle auto-framing when driving sheep toward narrow gates and bridges.

worst_problems.problem: The core season is only ten short evenings (roughly 2 to 3 minutes each), making the total runtime feel closer to a modest demo than a full ten-dollar release.
worst_problems.suggestion: Include procedural endless trials, community courses, or a seasonal career mode to sustain replay value.

boredom_points: Chasing down a single stray sheep that bolted off toward the corner of the map while the rest of the flock idles at the gate.
Replaying cleared evenings purely to grind stars for modest stat boosts like '+8% run speed'.
confusions: How the flanking keys (Z and X) orient Pip relative to the flock versus the player camera.
Why the Quiet Dog ribbon didn't show as unlocked on the post-game map screen despite getting three stars on Evening 1.
wish_list: Full controller support with analog triggers for trot vs. sprint.
A free-herding sandbox or peaceful pasture mode with no timers and no wolves.
Whistle audio cues mapped to directional commands like in actual sheepdog trials.
one_line_review: A mechanically authentic, quietly charming sheepdog sim that respects the craft of herding, held back only by clunky keyboard controls and a brief campaign.
